SyncLevel.doc: Durability/throughput tradeoff for WAL fsync discipline. Canonical home is wal because every fsync site lives here; the user-facing `PRAGMA synchronous` surface (parts/compiler/parts/statements/pragma) is a thin re-import. Closed enum; encoding is fixed (Off=0, Normal=1, Full=2, Extra=3) per the on-the-wire pragma surface — `PRAGMA synchronous = 2` and `PRAGMA synchronous = FULL` both yield SyncLevel::Full. Storage callers obtain the level via connection_get_synchronous(state) and pass it through wal_commit_with_sync; see master.md §fsync-discipline.

WalError.doc: Single failure channel for WAL operations. Targets map to idiomatic error types; the `message` field is human-readable for tests and logs.

WalHeader.doc: 32-byte WAL file header (mainline-compatible). magic_number selects checksum endianness: 0x377F0682 = little-endian u32 reads, 0x377F0683 = big-endian. file_format_version is fixed at 3007000. page_size mirrors the database's page_size; mismatch is a corruption signal. checkpoint_sequence increments on every checkpoint. salt_1/salt_2 are random 32-bit values that roll on every checkpoint, used to invalidate frames written before the most recent checkpoint. checksum_1/checksum_2 are the Fibonacci-style cumulative checksum over bytes 0..24 with initial state (0, 0) — they ALSO seed the running checksum used to validate frames.

WalFrameHeader.doc: 24-byte per-frame header (mainline-compatible). page_number is 1-based. db_size_after_commit is the COMMIT MARKER: nonzero only on the last frame of a transaction, giving the database size in pages after the transaction commits; zero on every interior frame. salt_1/salt_2 mirror the WAL header's current salts at write time; mismatch on read means the frame predates the last checkpoint and is dead. checksum_1/checksum_2 are the cumulative running checksum through this frame, starting from the WAL header's checksum and consuming each frame's (page_number, db_size_after_commit, page_image) bytes in order.

WalFrame.doc: One WAL frame: header + full page image. The page image is exactly page_size bytes; targets MUST NOT pad or truncate.

WalState.doc: In-memory state for a WAL session. page_size and salts are copies of the WAL header for fast reference. mx_frame is the frame number of the latest committed frame visible at this point in time; readers snapshot it at session open. wal_index maps page_number to the latest frame_number in [1, mx_frame] that wrote that page (latest-write-wins); used for O(1) page lookup. checkpoint_sequence mirrors the header for sanity checks.

WalIndexEntry.doc: Entry in the in-process wal_index. (page_number, frame_number) — frame_number is 1-based, latest-write-wins per page.

WalCommitInfo.doc: Returned by wal_commit. frames_written is how many frames this transaction appended; new_mx_frame is the post-commit mx_frame value (caller may discard, since WalState is mutated in place); db_size_after_commit echoes the value baked into the commit frame.

wal_open.doc: Open or create the WAL file at `{db_path}-wal`. If the file is shorter than 32 bytes, write a fresh header with random salts, checkpoint_sequence = 0, and the supplied page_size; return WalState with mx_frame = 0. Otherwise decode the header, validate its checksum, then scan frames forward — validating salts and the cumulative checksum — and set mx_frame to the largest frame number with db_size_after_commit != 0 among the prefix of valid frames. Build wal_index from frames 1..=mx_frame (latest-write-wins). Returns err(WalError) if the on-disk header is corrupt and cannot be reset, or if the page_size argument disagrees with an existing valid header.

wal_append_frame.doc: Append a frame to the in-progress transaction. Buffers (or eagerly writes — target choice) the frame at offset 32 + ((mx_frame + pending_count) * (24 + page_size)). The frame's salt fields copy state.salt_1/salt_2; checksum_1/checksum_2 extend the cumulative checksum from the prior frame's running state. db_size_after_commit is set to 0 (interior frame). The page image MUST be exactly state.page_size bytes; otherwise err(WalError).

wal_commit.doc: Finalize the in-progress transaction with FULL durability (unconditional fsync). Equivalent to wal_commit_with_sync(state, db_path, new_db_size, SyncLevel::Full). Preserved as a convenience wrapper for direct WAL tests; production callers (the wal-bridge pager) MUST use wal_commit_with_sync to honor the connection's PRAGMA synchronous level per the §fsync discipline matrix.

wal_commit_with_sync.doc: Finalize the in-progress transaction with explicit fsync gating. Rewrites the LAST pending frame's db_size_after_commit field to new_db_size and recomputes its checksum_1/checksum_2 with the new value baked in. Flushes all pending frames to the WAL file (single contiguous write at offset 32 + mx_frame * (24 + page_size)). Calls fsync iff sync_level >= Full per the W15/W16/W18 pins. Updates state.mx_frame and state.wal_index. Returns WalCommitInfo. Returns err(WalError) if no frames are pending OR if I/O fails. The fsync gate matrix (normative): Off → no fsync; Normal → no fsync (mainline-WAL default); Full → fsync; Extra → fsync. Used by pager_commit_transaction in the wal-bridge leaf to honor PRAGMA synchronous.

wal_rollback.doc: Discard the in-progress transaction. Drops any buffered pending frames; if any pending frames already reached the WAL file, they will be invalidated naturally because no commit frame follows them and they fall past mx_frame. Idempotent if no transaction is in progress.

wal_read_page.doc: Look up a page in the WAL by page_number. Returns Some(page_image) if wal_index contains the page (i.e. the latest frame for it within [1, mx_frame] exists in the live region), None otherwise — the caller falls back to the main database file. The returned image is exactly page_size bytes.

wal_checkpoint.doc: Fold all committed frames in [1, mx_frame] into the main database file at db_path, then reset the WAL header in place (bump checkpoint_sequence, roll salts to fresh random values, recompute header checksum). Sets state.mx_frame = 0 and clears wal_index. Does NOT truncate the WAL file (PASSIVE checkpoint semantics — old frames become invalid via salt mismatch, will be overwritten by next writer). Returns err(WalError) if I/O fails partway; the database file may be partially updated but the WAL header is rewritten LAST so a crash mid-checkpoint leaves the WAL still authoritative for unflushed frames.

wal_state_index_len.doc: Pin 18.2 sibling-target observer. Returns the number of entries in `state.wal_index`. Public accessor so callers (e.g. wal-bridge recovery-on-open) can iterate the WAL index without reaching into the record's representation. Targets that expose `wal_index` as a public field MAY also expose this for parity.

wal_state_index_entry.doc: Pin 18.2 sibling-target observer. Returns the i-th entry of `state.wal_index` (0-based, `i < wal_state_index_len(state)`). Companion to `wal_state_index_len` for recovery-on-open cache priming where targets without exposed-field access need a fn-form accessor. Returns `option<WalIndexEntry>` so out-of-range indices are signaled cleanly.

wal_checksum_step.doc: One step of the Fibonacci-style cumulative checksum. (s0', s1') = ((s0 + x0 + s1) mod 2^32, (s1 + x1 + s0') mod 2^32). Pure function; targets MAY inline this. Exposed in the shape surface so cross-target equivalence tests can call it directly with known vectors.

wal_encode_header.doc: Encode a WalHeader struct into the canonical 32 big-endian bytes. checksum_1/checksum_2 in the input header MUST already be valid (computed by the caller via wal_checksum_step over bytes 0..24); this function does not recompute. Used both for fresh-WAL creation and for checkpoint salt-roll.

wal_decode_header.doc: Decode 32 bytes into a WalHeader and validate its checksum. Returns err(WalError) on checksum mismatch, on unknown magic, or on file_format_version != 3007000. Does NOT validate page_size against any external value; the caller does that.

wal_encode_frame_header.doc: Encode a WalFrameHeader into the canonical 24 big-endian bytes. checksum fields in the input MUST already be valid; this function does not recompute.

wal_decode_frame_header.doc: Decode 24 bytes into a WalFrameHeader. Does NOT validate the cumulative checksum — that's the caller's job (the caller has the running state). Does NOT validate salts. Returns the raw header for the caller to validate against context.
